technical_and_design_decisions: All new modules will adhere to Spring Integration's standard module structure, public API conventions, and configuration patterns to ensure compatibility with existing Spring Integration applications and consistency with the framework's ecosystem.

The global error channel implementation (U7) will extend Spring Integration's built-in ErrorChannel and ErrorMessage support rather than replacing core error handling logic to maintain full backward compatibility with existing applications.
AWS-related modules (U2, U4) will use the AWS SDK for Java v2, the current supported version for official Spring Integration AWS extensions, to ensure long-term support and compatibility.
The Cassandra sink (U3) will use the DataStax Java Driver 4.x, the current supported driver for Cassandra 4.0+ which aligns with Spring Framework 6.0's Java 17+ baseline.
The HAWQ sink (U5) will use Apache Avro and Parquet libraries for serialization as specified, and the official PXF client for connectivity to HAWQ clusters.
The Solr sink (U6) will use Spring Data Solr to abstract Solr client interactions, ensuring consistency with the Spring ecosystem and reducing custom client code.
The existing partition strategy implementation from the GA release will be reused as-is for U8 testing, with no modifications to core strategy logic to avoid introducing regressions.
All new modules will be compatible with Spring Framework 6.0+ and Java 17+, matching the framework's current baseline requirements.
assumptions: The existing Spring Integration core codebase and public extension APIs are accessible and can be extended without modification to implement the new modules and error handling features.

The reference implementations linked in the specification (Spring Integration WebSocket, Spring Integration AWS) are approved for reuse of code patterns, configuration structures, and best practices to reduce development time and ensure consistency.

All required third-party dependencies (AWS SDK v2, DataStax Cassandra driver, PXF client, Spring Data Solr, Avro/Parquet libraries) are compatible with Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6.0, and are available in the project's dependency management system.

The custom exception hierarchy (GlobalException, DefaultException, ModuleSpecificException) referenced in U7 is already defined in the project's shared common module, so no new exception classes need to be created for this increment.
Test environments for all external systems (WebSocket clients, AWS S3/SES, Cassandra, HAWQ, Solr) are available and accessible for integration testing during development.
The existing partition strategy implementation from the GA release has stable public APIs that allow for test harness development to simulate module add/remove operations without modifying core code.

No changes to existing Spring Integration core functionality are required to implement the requested features; all work is limited to new module development and extension of existing error handling infrastructure.

activities.activity_description: Design and develop a reusable Spring Integration WebSocket inbound source module that ingests browser-based events via WebSocket, converts events to Spring Integration Message objects, and routes them to a configurable message channel, including configuration properties for endpoint setup and connection handling.

Develop a Spring Integration AWS source module supporting two ingestion patterns: polling for new objects from Amazon S3, and receiving inbound emails via Amazon SES, using AWS SDK for Java v2, with configurable properties for both source types and error handling.

Develop a Spring Integration Cassandra sink module that writes message payloads to a Cassandra NoSQL database, optimized for high-volume write throughput, using the DataStax Java Driver, with configurable connection, consistency, and write settings.

Develop a Spring Integration AWS sink module that writes message payloads to Amazon S3, using AWS SDK for Java v2, with configurable bucket, path, object naming, and ACL settings, following existing Spring Integration AWS extension patterns.

Develop a Spring Integration HAWQ sink module that writes message payloads to HAWQ via PXF extensions, with support for Avro and Parquet serialization formats as specified, including configurable PXF connection, format, and write settings.

Develop a Spring Integration Solr sink module that indexes message payloads to a Solr backend server for full-text search, using Spring Data Solr, with configurable Solr connection, core, and indexing settings.

Extend Spring Integration's existing error handling infrastructure to implement a configurable global error channel, propagate full exception hierarchy (including nested Caused by chains) as error message payloads, add support for custom exception filtering via catch configuration, and ensure all errors from custom and built-in source/processor/sink modules are routed to the configured error channel.

Develop and execute integration tests to validate that the existing GA release partition strategy dynamically adapts to module additions and removals from the integration flow, with no data loss or message misrouting, as specified in U8.

Develop and execute end-to-end integration tests for all new source and sink modules, validate error channel routing across all module types, and verify partition strategy behavior with all new modules integrated into test flows.

Create user-facing documentation for all new source/sink modules and the global error channel feature, including configuration examples, usage guidelines, and references to the provided Spring Integration extension examples.
